title: A high-frequency lamella proves cutoff-exponent sharpness

sharpness_control.construction: Fix 0<alpha<1 and choose integers M_N with alpha N<=M_N<=N; set f_N(x)=sin(M_N x_1) on normalized T3
sharpness_control.bandlimit: The only nonzero Fourier modes of f_N are plus/minus M_N e_1, so f_N is degree N
sharpness_control.sign_shell: sgn(sin(M_N x_1)) has Fourier mass 8/pi^2 in its fundamental pair plus/minus M_N e_1, hence H_(alpha,N)>=8/pi^2
sharpness_control.phase_balance: The positive and negative phases each have normalized volume one half
sharpness_control.defect: int(f_N^2-1)^2=int cos(M_N x_1)^4=3/8 for every N
sharpness_control.sharpness: K1554's N^0 cutoff exponent is attained up to constants by a fixed-shell family; no lower bound growing with N can hold under only the declared normalized hypotheses
sharpness_control.scope_guard: The example proves sharpness only in the cutoff exponent and does not identify the optimal c_(alpha,eta), a low-energy likelihood, Fisher cost or the ground-state profile
